metadata.title: FORGE OS — 18-Month Engineering Roadmap
metadata.schedule: Five focused learning days, Day 6 weekly checkpoint/lab, Day 7 light review/catch-up. One primary item per day.
metadata.workload: 100–160 minutes on focused days, 150–180 minutes for checkpoints, 45–60 minutes for weekly review.
metadata.dsaCadence: Two dedicated DSA sessions weekly plus two short spaced-recall sessions; DSA continues through all six phases.
principles: Start from the learner's existing HTML/CSS/React/Node/MongoDB/Python/Git knowledge; use diagnostic tasks and avoid re-teaching demonstrated skills.
Prioritise independent implementation, debugging, tests, retrieval practice and explanation over passive course completion.
Use existing e-commerce app as the flagship backend project, especially cart, checkout, orders and inventory logic.
Integrate OS, DBMS, Computer Networks, OOP and Computer Architecture into the learning sequence; no academic dashboard.
Treat Gram Setu and Border Sentinel as prior portfolio assets; do not rebuild them by default.
No fake completion; every daily topic and milestone begins incomplete.

metadata.calendarNote: 78 full weekly curriculum records run from 2026-11-16 through 2028-05-14 (journey days 1-546). Day 547 is a separate final showcase on 2028-05-15, preserving the existing application target date. The exact 18-calendar-month date is 2028-05-16.
metadata.itemIdStrategy: journey_day_NNN; stable and unique across the complete roadmap.
metadata.milestoneMapping: Each milestone has a non-overlapping inclusive journey-day range and requiredItemIds. Runtime milestone completion is derived from CurriculumProgress, never manually toggled.
metadata.subtopicMapping: Original subtopic text is preserved in subtopics; subtopicItems adds stable IDs for database and UI checkboxes.
metadata.performanceNote: Import CurriculumItem records once using bulkWrite. Do not pre-create all DailyPlan documents; create only a requested date plan.

milestones.title: Programming baseline validated
milestones.tagline: You can reason about code, not just run it.
milestones.description: Demonstrate working JavaScript fundamentals, a reliable C++ setup and basic complexity reasoning.
topicsCovered: JavaScript values, control flow and functions
acceptanceCriteria: Complete the initial diagnostic and document gaps.
Write small JavaScript and C++ programs independently.
Explain the complexity of a simple traversal, nested loop and search.
Use Git branches and meaningful commits.
milestones.progressRule: Complete when every required daily curriculum item in this range is completed.

milestones.title: Browser-side JavaScript engineer
milestones.tagline: You understand the browser runtime and asynchronous code.
milestones.description: Build browser features using DOM events, storage, async APIs and TypeScript foundations.
topicsCovered: DOM, event delegation and browser storage
acceptanceCriteria: Build a browser utility with dynamic DOM interactions and persistence.
Handle API loading, failure, timeout and cancellation.
Explain one event-loop output trace and one closure example.
Use TypeScript types for data boundaries.
milestones.progressRule: Complete when every required daily curriculum item in this range is completed.

milestones.title: Frontend engineer: React + TypeScript release
milestones.tagline: A deployed interface with maintainable state and tests.
milestones.description: Ship a polished multi-route React/TypeScript application and demonstrate foundational DSA.
topicsCovered: Arrays, strings, hashing, search, trees and graph fundamentals
acceptanceCriteria: Deploy the API Explorer with list/detail routes.
Support loading, empty, error, search and filter states.
Pass build, typecheck, lint and critical component tests.
Solve unseen foundational DSA problems and explain complexity.
milestones.progressRule: Complete when every required daily curriculum item in this range is completed.

milestones.title: Backend foundations: Node, Express and MongoDB
milestones.tagline: You can design and implement backend business logic.
milestones.description: Build secure API boundaries, intentional data models and the first complete cart flow.
topicsCovered: Express routing, middleware and error handling
acceptanceCriteria: Explain the Node request/event-loop model.
Implement controllers that delegate business rules to services.
Enforce user ownership and validate all inputs.
Demonstrate persistent add/update/remove cart operations.
milestones.progressRule: Complete when every required daily curriculum item in this range is completed.

milestones.title: Full-stack E-commerce V1
milestones.tagline: A complete product, cart and order journey.
milestones.description: Finish the existing e-commerce project instead of abandoning it for another tutorial.
acceptanceCriteria: A user can browse products, log in, manage a persistent cart and create an order.
Server-side logic recalculates prices and validates stock.
Duplicate checkout and invalid quantities are handled safely.
Critical routes have automated tests and a documented API.
milestones.progressRule: Complete when every required daily curriculum item in this range is completed.

milestones.title: Reliable backend primitives
milestones.tagline: Your API handles shared state and asynchronous work.
milestones.description: Use TypeScript, automated tests, Redis, rate limits and background jobs in one real service.
topicsCovered: Redis data structures and cache invalidation
acceptanceCriteria: A backend feature is fully typed and runtime-validated.
Critical business rules and API flows are tested.
Redis-backed caching or rate limiting works and is measured.
A background job retries safely without duplicate side effects.
milestones.progressRule: Complete when every required daily curriculum item in this range is completed.

milestones.title: Production-oriented backend V2
milestones.tagline: Build, test, containerise and observe your service.
milestones.description: Harden the e-commerce backend with Docker, CI, performance measurements and advanced DSA.
topicsCovered: Graph algorithms, DSU, MST and DP
acceptanceCriteria: The service runs from a reproducible Docker Compose setup.
CI runs lint, typecheck, tests and build.
Redis and queue features have failure-path tests.
One performance improvement is measured before and after.
Advanced DSA implementations are explained and tested.
milestones.progressRule: Complete when every required daily curriculum item in this range is completed.

milestones.title: Java and object-oriented design
milestones.tagline: You can model domain behaviour in Java.
milestones.description: Demonstrate Java language fluency, composition, interfaces, collections and concurrency basics.
acceptanceCriteria: Build a tested Java domain model with clear invariants.
Choose collections based on access patterns.
Demonstrate and fix a race condition.
Explain one meaningful design trade-off.
milestones.progressRule: Complete when every required daily curriculum item in this range is completed.

milestones.title: Secure Spring Boot API
milestones.tagline: A relational backend with tests and access control.
milestones.description: Implement Spring Boot REST endpoints backed by PostgreSQL and JPA.
acceptanceCriteria: CRUD endpoints use DTOs and service boundaries.
Database relations and transactions behave correctly.
Validation and consistent errors are implemented.
Authentication and resource permissions are tested.
milestones.progressRule: Complete when every required daily curriculum item in this range is completed.

milestones.title: System design and Spring service capstone
milestones.tagline: You can explain how your service behaves under load and failure.
milestones.description: Release an Inventory and Order Management API with explicit system-design trade-offs.
topicsCovered: Timeouts, circuit breakers and graceful degradation
acceptanceCriteria: Release a documented Spring Boot inventory/order service.
Present one-page architecture and API diagrams.
Explain database, caching and messaging trade-offs.
Demonstrate one timeout/retry or idempotency behaviour.
Complete a system-design walkthrough.
milestones.progressRule: Complete when every required daily curriculum item in this range is completed.

milestones.title: Core systems and networking foundation
milestones.tagline: You understand what happens below the API.
milestones.description: Connect Linux operations, computer architecture, OS concepts and network protocols to application behaviour.
acceptanceCriteria: Use shell tools to inspect processes, logs and permissions.
Explain binary representation, CPU execution and cache locality.
Explain virtual memory, scheduling and concurrency.
Trace DNS, TCP and HTTPS at a high level.
milestones.progressRule: Complete when every required daily curriculum item in this range is completed.

milestones.title: Cloud-deployed application
milestones.tagline: You can deploy a containerised service with secure cloud boundaries.
milestones.description: Deploy a service with a clear network, identity, storage and database plan.
acceptanceCriteria: Deploy a versioned container image in a budget-controlled environment.
Keep the database private and credentials outside the repository.
Document health checks, logs, backups and teardown.
Recreate the deployment from written instructions.
milestones.progressRule: Complete when every required daily curriculum item in this range is completed.

milestones.title: DevOps and reliability capstone
milestones.tagline: You can operate and recover a deployed application.
milestones.description: Demonstrate CI/CD, basic Kubernetes, Kafka concepts and observability without unnecessary complexity.
acceptanceCriteria: CI/CD gates a deployment on successful quality checks.
A local Kubernetes deployment can be rolled out and rolled back.
A producer/consumer demo handles retries and duplicate events.
The application has basic metrics/logs and a recovery runbook.
milestones.progressRule: Complete when every required daily curriculum item in this range is completed.

milestones.title: Machine learning engineering foundation
milestones.tagline: You can train and evaluate a model responsibly.
milestones.description: Build a leakage-safe, reproducible ML pipeline and a small neural network.
topicsCovered: Linear algebra and probability for ML
acceptanceCriteria: Build a reproducible dataset and training pipeline.
Compare multiple baselines using appropriate metrics.
Explain data leakage and overfitting.
Train and evaluate a small PyTorch model.
milestones.progressRule: Complete when every required daily curriculum item in this range is completed.

milestones.title: LLM retrieval engineer
milestones.tagline: You can build grounded answers from a document collection.
milestones.description: Run local models and construct vector retrieval and a basic cited RAG system.
acceptanceCriteria: Run a local model through a documented API.
Ingest a curated document collection with source metadata.
Retrieve relevant chunks and produce source-linked answers.
Record latency and retrieval-quality measurements.
milestones.progressRule: Complete when every required daily curriculum item in this range is completed.

milestones.title: AI research capstone
milestones.tagline: You can design, evaluate and explain a complete AI system.
milestones.description: Ship a RAG/agent application or approved research extension with reproducible evaluation.
acceptanceCriteria: Deliver a working end-to-end AI application.
Evaluate on a curated test set with documented metrics.
Compare at least one baseline and one improved variant.
Include failure examples, limitations and setup instructions.
Publish a short technical report and demo.
milestones.progressRule: Complete when every required daily curriculum item in this range is completed.

milestones.title: 18-month engineering showcase
milestones.tagline: Show what you can build and explain independently.
milestones.description: Final portfolio review on 15 May 2028, the 18-month anniversary of the journey start.
acceptanceCriteria: Present three strongest projects with demos and READMEs.
Explain architecture, data model, testing and deployment choices.
Complete a final DSA/Core CS self-assessment.
Write a realistic next six-month learning and internship plan.
milestones.progressRule: Complete when the final portfolio showcase is completed.

projects.name: Browser API Lab
projects.purpose: Apply async JavaScript, DOM events, browser storage and network error handling.
requirements: Search/filter a real public API or local JSON dataset
Loading, empty, error, retry and timeout states
Persist a small user preference or saved list
acceptanceCriteria: Works without a tutorial during a short walkthrough
Handles malformed and empty responses
No unsafe HTML injection
README explains architecture and edge cases

projects.name: Developer Resource API Explorer
projects.purpose: Demonstrate React/TypeScript frontend engineering without rebuilding another generic todo app.
requirements: Search, filter, sort and URL query state
Loading, error, empty and retry states
acceptanceCriteria: Fresh clone setup documented
Build/typecheck/lint/tests pass
Responsive and keyboard-usable
Deployed demo plus architecture note

projects.name: Existing E-commerce Application — V1
projects.purpose: Finish the user's existing incomplete e-commerce project, especially the cart controller logic.
acceptanceCriteria: A complete browse-to-order journey works end-to-end
Cart persists across refresh and login
No client-submitted price is trusted
Concurrent checkout cannot silently oversell inventory
Critical routes have tests

projects.name: E-commerce Backend — Production V2
projects.purpose: Upgrade the flagship backend with type safety, testing, caching, queues and deployment discipline.
requirements: Migrate one vertical slice to strict TypeScript
acceptanceCriteria: Fresh clone can run the stack from documented commands
Critical flows pass tests
Cache/queue failure paths are handled
One performance change is measured
Secrets are not committed or baked into images

projects.name: Inventory and Order Management API
projects.purpose: Build a clean Java service to demonstrate OOP, Spring and relational data design.
acceptanceCriteria: CRUD and order workflows work against PostgreSQL
Transactions and locking behaviour are tested
Security checks prevent unauthorised updates
Architecture diagram and API documentation are complete

projects.name: Cloud Operations Capstone
projects.purpose: Operate one existing backend service in a repeatable, observable, cost-controlled environment.
requirements: Least-privilege cloud identity and network boundaries
Kubernetes local deployment and rollback lab
Logs, metrics, SLO and recovery runbook
acceptanceCriteria: Deployment can be recreated and torn down from instructions
Database is not publicly exposed
CI blocks bad builds
Failure/recovery drill is demonstrated
Costs and security assumptions are documented

projects.name: Forge Research Companion
projects.purpose: Build a grounded assistant for a curated collection of technical PDFs and research papers.
requirements: Ingest a curated set of technical PDFs/text files
Return cited answers and abstain when evidence is missing
Evaluate retrieval and answer quality on a labelled test set
Add bounded tool calling with step limits and logs
Benchmark latency and document compute requirements
acceptanceCriteria: Every answer citation resolves to a source passage
The system can say it does not know
A labelled test set reports retrieval metrics
At least one baseline and improved variant are compared
Failure cases and limitations are documented
README, architecture diagram and demo are complete
projects.optionalResearchExtension: If choosing to continue Border Sentinel, replace only the final capstone domain with a narrowly scoped CV experiment (e.g. low-light detection/tracking robustness) with a fixed dataset, baseline, metrics and ablation. Do not attempt both capstones simultaneously.
